lesson_title: Percent Means Out of a Hundred
hook_text: Up 25%, then down 25%. Back where you started? Nope.
clip_script: Watch the trap: an increase of twenty-five percent followed by a decrease of twenty-five percent does NOT return to the start. 640 rises to 800, but twenty-five percent of 800 is 200, so it falls to 600. The second percentage is taken of a different, larger amount.
visual_style: A bar of 640 learners grows by a quarter to 800, then a larger quarter is cut away leaving 600, with the starting line shown for comparison.
pacing: Quick rise, dramatic fall, pause on the gap.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to calculate any percentage in your head with the ten-percent method.
